title: PolyFormer: Scalable Node-wise Filters via Polynomial Graph Transformer

problem.claim: Shared polynomial coefficients produce node-unified filters whose flexibility is limited for node-level tasks.

gap.claim: Existing node-wise filtering with positional encoding has burdensome initialization and updating that hinder scalability on large-scale graphs.

contributions.claim: PolyAttn is a scalable node-wise filter that directly learns node-wise filters using attention.
PolyFormer is a Graph Transformer model built on PolyAttn that calculates attention scores within nodes and captures spectral information.
The proposed model targets node-level tasks on both homophilic and heterophilic graphs.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that PolyFormer achieves a desirable balance between scalability and expressiveness for node-level tasks.
The authors report superior performance on homophilic and heterophilic graphs and successful handling of graphs with up to 100 million nodes.
The authors report that the methods excel at learning arbitrary node-wise filters.

narrative_sequence.summary: Spectral Graph Neural Networks perform strongly in graph representation learning.
Node-unified polynomial filters limit flexibility, while positional-encoding-based node-wise filters hinder scalability.
The work proposes PolyAttn to learn node-wise filters directly and efficiently through attention.
PolyFormer builds on PolyAttn as a scalable Graph Transformer that captures spectral information.
The authors report strong node-wise filtering performance across graph types and scalability to graphs with up to 100 million nodes.
